claims.evidence: Photo shows chair reclined almost flat, which could match 'bent' as a recline feature, but the word could also imply frame damage; no close-up of frame confirms either reading.

risks.risk: Recline and height-adjustment mechanisms may not lock or function properly
risks.proof: Short video showing the lever being used to raise/lower seat and lock the recline at different angles

risks.risk: Caster wheels may be damaged, seized, or missing
risks.proof: Close-up photo/video of all five wheels rolling on a hard floor

risks.risk: Mesh back may have tears, sagging, or stains not visible from the front angle
risks.proof: Photo of the back and underside of the seat and mesh panel

risks.risk: Armrests or headrest pad may be loose, cracked, or detached
risks.proof: Photo/video showing armrests and headrest being pressed or moved

risks.risk: Possible structural bend or crack in frame/base implied by seller's wording
risks.proof: Clear photo of the full frame, base, and gas cylinder from multiple angles, plus seller clarifying what 'bent' means
risks.if_unproven: priced as having a structural defect

risks.risk: Unknown age and duration of prior use affecting overall wear
risks.proof: Seller statement with purchase date or receipt, or close-up of wear points (seat edges, armrest pads)
risks.if_unproven: priced as heavily used, older stock

proof_requests: Video of the chair reclining and height lever in use
Close-up of all caster wheels rolling on hard floor
Photos of chair back, underside, and mesh panel for tears/stains
Clarification of what 'bent' refers to, with photos of frame/base from multiple angles
Photo/video testing armrest and headrest stability
response.reason: The witness clearly identifies a reclining mesh office chair, so it can be priced at worst case given the unverified mechanical condition, wheel wear, and the ambiguous 'bent' claim, pending further proof.
